headline: A 2021 House bill would have barred the Department of Veterans Affairs from charging veterans for contraceptives that insurance plans must cover without cost-sharing.
what_it_does: The bill would have prohibited the Department of Veterans Affairs from requiring veterans to pay for any contraceptive item that health insurance plans are required to cover with no cost-sharing. It would have applied to VA care in that way. The House voted it down on June 15, 2021, so it was not adopted.

who_it_affects.group: veterans who receive health care through the Department of Veterans Affairs
who_it_affects.how: They would not have had to pay out of pocket for contraceptive items that private insurance plans must cover without cost-sharing.
It would have been barred from requiring payment from veterans for those covered contraceptive items.
